title: Normalized affine transitivity comparisons and stalk right exactness
statement: Let X, Y, S be schemes [def-pc-scheme], h:X→Y and g:Y→S morphisms, and q:Ω_{X/S}→Ω_{X/Y} a morphism of O_X-modules [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] sending d_{X/S}a to d_{X/Y}a on every source open. Use the actual tensor-pullback differential map u:h*Ω_{Y/S}→Ω_{X/S} [def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map, def-pc-module-pullback]. Then: (i) at every x∈X the maps u_x,q_x on module stalks [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] are exact and q_x is surjective; (ii) for every affine triple U=Spec A⊆X,V=Spec B⊆Y,W=Spec R⊆S with h(U)⊆V and g(V)⊆W there is an isomorphism θ:(h*Ω_{Y/S})|_{Spec A} ≅ tilde(A⊗_B Ω_{B/R}), carrying the restriction of each actual pulled-back db to the canonical section of 1⊗db. There are A-linear maps u_A:A⊗_B Ω_{B/R}→Ω_{A/R} and v_A:Ω_{A/R}→Ω_{A/B}, with u_A(a⊗db)=a d(h♯b) and v_A(da)=da, exact with v_A surjective. Under θ and the fixed relativeDifferentialsRestrictFromSpecIso comparisons, the restrictions of u and q are precisely tilde(u_A) and tilde(v_A). All comparisons are sheaf isomorphisms and hence include their restriction maps. No additional hypotheses on h or g are imposed.

source.place: Tag 01UX, lemma-triangle-differentials, first proof; affine description Tag 01UT, functoriality Tag 01UV; localized exactness Algebra Tag 00CS

proof.text: Fix affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Y$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ with $h(U)\subset V$ and $g(V)\subset W$. Such triples cover $X$: choose $W$ about $gh(x)$, then affine $V$ about $h(x)$ inside $g^{-1}W$, then affine $U$ about $x$ inside $h^{-1}V$. By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] the middle and last terms on $U$ are the associated sheaves of $\Omega_{A/R}$ and $\Omega_{A/B}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-chart-unit] (with $f=h$, $G=\Omega_{Y/S}$) the restriction of $h^*\Omega_{Y/S}$ to $U$ is identified with $\psi^*(\Omega_{Y/S}|_V)$, $\psi:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, carrying the pulled-back section $\eta_h(s)|_U$ to $\eta_\psi(s)$ for $s\in\Omega_{Y/S}(V)$; by naturality of this comparison in $G$, the affine description $\Omega_{Y/S}|_V\cong\widetilde{\Omega_{B/R}}$ transports it. Then apply [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] with the ring map $B\to A$ and module $\Omega_{B/R}$. It identifies the first term with $\widetilde{A\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R}}$ and the pulled-back $db$ with $1\otimes db$. By [def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map] and linearity the existing first arrow sends $a\otimes db$ to $a\,d(h^\sharp b)$. The supplied q also sends da to da. These elements generate: differentials are generated by $db$ in the quotient construction of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and tensors are sums of pure tensors. Thus this is precisely the associated first algebraic arrow, not an unspecified isomorphic arrow. The chart-unit theorem uses the ordinary pullback. The ordinary and tensor pullback functors are both left adjoint to the same pushforward; compare them by uniqueness of left adjoints. Its unit identity carries the explicit tensor unit to the ordinary pullback unit. Inserting this comparison into the affine-chart route and the tensor-tilde comparison supplies the required normalized θ, without choosing an unnormalized isomorphism.

proof.text: On each triple take the algebraic second arrow v:Ω_{A/R}→Ω_{A/B}, da↦da, from [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-first-exact-sequence]. Since q sends every da to da, the canonical differential affine comparisons identify q with tilde(v): the elements da generate and the comparisons preserve the derivations. The same argument on a tensor db identifies the canonical first arrow with tilde(u), using the normalization of θ in step 1. Both maps commute with principal localization by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization]. On inverted elements the forced rule is d(a/t^n)=t^{-n}da-na t^{-n-1}dt. Thus these are equalities of sheaf arrows, not just choices of isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 01UX, lemma-triangle-differentials; restriction Tag 01US, lemma-differentials-restrict-open; affine Tag 01UT

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-first-exact-sequence] to $R\to B\to A$: write its first two maps as $u,v$. It gives $vu=0$, $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$, and surjectivity of $v$, without any finiteness or flatness assumption. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], the stalk maps of the associated arrows at a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ are exactly the localized maps (on a germ of a global element they apply $u$ or $v$, and every stalk element is a fraction of such a germ). Exactness survives here by the explicit fraction argument: if $v(m)/s=0$, choose $t\notin\mathfrak p$ with $t v(m)=0$; write $tm=u(l)$; then $m/s=u(l)/(ts)$. Conversely $vu=0$ remains zero. If $n/s$ is in the last stalk, choose $m$ with $v(m)=n$; $m/s$ maps to $n/s$. Thus the displayed sheaf sequence is right exact on every stalk.

theorem relativeDifferentials_transitivity_affine_stalk
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (h : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (q : (h ≫ g).relativeDifferentials ⟶ h.relativeDifferentials)
    (hq : ∀ (O : X.Opens) (a : Γ(X, O)),
      q.app O ((h ≫ g).relativeDifferentialsDerivation.d (X := op O) a) =
        h.relativeDifferentialsDerivation.d (X := op O) a) :
      (∀ x : X,
        Function.Exact
          ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map
            (g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackMap h))
          ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map q) ∧
        Function.Surjective ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map q)) ∧
      (∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens) (W : S.affineOpens)
          (hUV : U.1 ≤ h ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) (hVW : V.1 ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ W.1),
        ∃ θ : ((Modules.tensorPullback h).obj g.relativeDifferentials).restrict U.2.fromSpec ≅
            tilde ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (h.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV).hom).obj
              (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential (g.appLE W.1 V.1 hVW))),
          (∀ b : Γ(Y, V.1),
            θ.hom.app ⊤
              ((Modules.sectionsRestrictFromSpecLinearEquiv
                ((Modules.tensorPullback h).obj g.relativeDifferentials) U.2).symm
                (((Modules.tensorPullback h).obj g.relativeDifferentials).presheaf.map
                  (homOfLE hUV).op (g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackGenerator h V.1 b))) =
              tilde.toOpen ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (h.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV).hom).obj
                (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential (g.appLE W.1 V.1 hVW))) ⊤
                  ((ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (h.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV).hom).unit.app
                    (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential (g.appLE W.1 V.1 hVW))
                      (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d b))) ∧
          ∃ (uA : (ModuleCat.extendScalars (h.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV).hom).obj
                (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential (g.appLE W.1 V.1 hVW)) ⟶
              CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential
                ((h ≫ g).appLE W.1 U.1 (fun _ hx ↦ hVW (hUV hx))))
            (vA : CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential
                ((h ≫ g).appLE W.1 U.1 (fun _ hx ↦ hVW (hUV hx))) ⟶
              CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential (h.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV)),
            (∀ (a : Γ(X, U.1)) (b : Γ(Y, V.1)),
              uA (a • @id
                ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (h.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV).hom).obj
                  (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential (g.appLE W.1 V.1 hVW)))
                ((ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (h.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV).hom).unit.app
                  (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential (g.appLE W.1 V.1 hVW))
                    (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d b))) =
                a • CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d (h.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV b)) ∧
            (∀ a : Γ(X, U.1), vA (CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d a) =
              CommRingCat.KaehlerDifferential.d a) ∧
            Function.Exact uA vA ∧ Function.Surjective vA ∧
            (Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.fromSpec).map
                (g.relativeDifferentialsPullbackMap h) ≫
              ((h ≫ g).relativeDifferentialsRestrictFromSpecIso W.2 U.2
                (fun _ hx ↦ hVW (hUV hx))).hom =
              θ.hom ≫ (tilde.functor Γ(X, U.1)).map uA ∧
            (Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.fromSpec).map q ≫
                (h.relativeDifferentialsRestrictFromSpecIso V.2 U.2 hUV).hom =
              ((h ≫ g).relativeDifferentialsRestrictFromSpecIso W.2 U.2
                (fun _ hx ↦ hVW (hUV hx))).hom ≫ (tilde.functor Γ(X, U.1)).map vA)
